title: Safety-Gymnasium: A Unified Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Velocity tasks deliberately make faster and therefore higher-reward behavior costly once the velocity safety constraint binds.
quote: Velocity-Constraint involves safety tasks using MuJoCo agents. In these tasks, agents aim for higher reward by moving faster, but they must also adhere to velocity constraints for safety.

title: Safety-Gymnasium: A Unified Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Across benchmark experiments reward and episodic cost move in a trade-off, with unconstrained reward maximization producing risky behavior.
quote: Episodic reward and cost exhibit a trade-off relationship. Unconstrained algorithms aim to maximize reward through risky behaviors.

title: Safety-Gymnasium: A Unified Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Navigation tasks with greater stochasticity exhibit pronounced oscillations in safe-RL performance.
quote: However, pronounced oscillations are present in navigation tasks characterized by high stochasticity.

title: Safety-Gymnasium: A Unified Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Lagrangian multiplier learning rates that are too large cause oscillation while rates that are too small slow convergence.
quote: A high learning rate induces excessive oscillations, impedes convergence speed, and hinders the algorithm’s ability to attain the desired solution. Conversely, a low learning rate slows down convergence and adversely affects training.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: CRAX deliberately constructs tasks in which increased performance generally incurs more cost and safety requires sacrificing reward.
quote: Each task defines reward and cost signals, inducing a trade-off between performance and safety: achieving high reward typically requires incurring higher cost, while satisfying safety constraints necessitates sacrificing some reward.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Direct training on the hardest contexts often fails to find good policies because exploration is dominated by violations and sparse progress.
quote: when trained directly on the hardest difficulty level, agents often struggle to discover a good policy, as exploration becomes dominated by constraint violations and sparse progress.

title: CRAX: Fast Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmarking
statement: Making the safety bound stricter produces an asymmetric and substantially larger performance loss.
environment: CRAX tasks with varied safety bounds
quote: Tightening the bound leads to a substantially larger drop in score than the gains obtained by increasing it by the same amount.

title: Responsive Safety in Reinforcement Learning by PID Lagrangian Methods
statement: Ordinary Lagrangian learning exhibits oscillation and overshoot that causes constraint violations during training.

title: Balance Reward and Safety Optimization for Safe Reinforcement Learning: A Perspective of Gradient Manipulation
statement: On velocity-constrained OmniSafe tasks established constrained baselines struggle to preserve safety while pursuing reward.
quote: SOTA baselines such as CUP and PPOLag struggle to ensure safety, and their reward performance is worse than our algorithm.

title: Safety Generalization Under Distribution Shift in Safe Reinforcement Learning: A Diabetes Testbed
statement: Policies satisfying training-patient safety constraints degrade and violate deployment criteria on patients with different physiological dynamics.
environment: Unified diabetes simulator, unseen patient contexts
quote: policies that achieve high TIR and low Risk Index on the training patients show substantial degradation when deployed on physiologically distinct patients.

title: Robust Constrained Reinforcement Learning
statement: Mismatch between training and deployment transition dynamics can cause performance degradation and constraint violation, motivating robust constrained policies.

title: Effects of Safety State Augmentation on Safe Exploration
statement: With ordinary episodic constraint feedback the learner only learns about violation after an episode, while safety-state augmentation supplies distance-to-violation information continuously.
environment: Pendulum swing-up and point-goal safe RL
quote: While an algorithm without the safety state will receive information on constraint violation after an episode, the safety state would constantly inform the algorithm of the distance toward a violation.

title: Towards a Practical Understanding of Lagrangian Methods in Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: Within the same Safety-Gymnasium task, changing the cost limit can change which Lagrange-multiplier update method is best.
environment: Eight Safety-Gymnasium navigation and velocity tasks
quote: there is no single method that consistently performs best within a task, but rather depends on the chosen cost limit.

title: Towards a Practical Understanding of Lagrangian Methods in Safe Reinforcement Learning
statement: The multiplier value appropriate for constraint satisfaction varies substantially with both the task and the selected cost limit.
environment: Eight Safety-Gymnasium navigation and velocity tasks
quote: This indicates that the optimal value λ* is highly task-dependent and dependent on the value of the cost limit.

title: GUARD: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Replacing static hazards with dynamic collision-inducing ghosts raises training variance for multiple constrained methods.
quote: These tasks exhibit higher variance during the training process due to the collision-inducing behaviors of the dynamic ghosts.

title: GUARD: A Safe Reinforcement Learning Benchmark
statement: Contexts with higher-dimensional robot action spaces and more complex workspaces converge more slowly.
environment: GUARD Walker and Arm task variants
quote: tasks that involve high-dimensional robot action spaces and complex workspaces suffer from slower convergence due to the increased complexity of the learning problem.
